claims.wording: Crossing Guard connects through hook entries for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor and a plugin for OpenCode. Claude Code and Codex can allow, hold or deny a tool call; Codex skips a hook until it is trusted; OpenCode blocks only on the verified version (1.18.0) and records otherwise; Cursor denies, and an ask is denied.
Memory is one Markdown file per record under ~/.crossing-guard/memory. Claude Code and Codex read the same store through a session-start hook installed with crossing-guard attach.

A rule is a JSON object with an id, an action and a condition. The actions are deny, ask, allow, observe and redact. A fresh install selects no rules, and the safety-starter rulebook has six. The git-force-push rule shown is copied from that file.
With the safety-starter rules, crossing-guard check printed an ASK line naming git-force-push for a force push to main, and an allow line with no rule matched for git status.
claims.versions: Local build of Crossing Guard source 1e89282b with Go 1.26; safety-starter rules selected through CG_RULES; macOS
claims.evidence_private_reason: Run by the maintainers on a local build of the published commit. The two commands are on the page, so anyone can repeat the run.

claims.wording: The daemon listens on a loopback address by default, and every API route requires a token.
The console drafts a handoff note from a session, a person edits it, and publishing writes it into the repository.
An ask rule holds the tool call for a person in a local approvals inbox, and the call is denied when the inbox cannot be reached or the request expires.
Each session's event log carries a sha256 hash chain, and crossing-guard chain verify recomputes it.
The console Usage view aggregates token counts from local session files (input, output, cache hit rate, per agent and per day) and holds no plan limit.

A managed helper, reviewer or follower run whose provider reports a quota, outage or sign-in error is retried on the same route up to three times, moved to the next user-authored route, then parked. A route names a runtime and a model. Verified by tests against a simulated provider.
